subject.title: [Bug]: Heartbeat / async system events can interrupt and effectively swallow in-progress replies in Telegram topic sessions

question: Should heartbeat and async system-event turns continue to run in user-facing main/topic sessions by default, or should they move to a non-authorizing, non-preemptive lane for active Telegram conversations except for explicit immediate/manual wakes?
rationale: Current code has partial guards, but the remaining behavior crosses compatibility-sensitive heartbeat defaults, delivery targets, stale final replay, and wrong-recipient confidentiality; automation should not choose that policy alone.

options.title: Define the non-preemptive heartbeat lane
options.body: Keep this issue open, resolve or supersede the linked narrow PRs, and implement a maintainer-approved heartbeat/system-event boundary with tests and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Prove current main and close later
options.body: Only close after maintainers provide current-main Telegram proof that active replies, stale final replay, default-target delivery, and deferred-maintenance lane symptoms are all fixed.

options.title: Preserve shared heartbeat behavior
options.body: Document the current main-session behavior and operator config workaround, accepting that some Telegram topic setups may need manual isolation settings.

recommendation.title: Define the non-preemptive heartbeat lane
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, resolve or supersede the linked narrow PRs, and implement a maintainer-approved heartbeat/system-event boundary with tests and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent adjacent product-boundary involvement and current local history points to Peter Steinberger on the central heartbeat runner snapshot.
